label: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
output:
Here's your announcement, ready to paste into the website and hand to the coffee shops and the library branch:

---

**FIX-IT SATURDAY AT ST. ANSGAR**
Saturday, December 5, 2026 · 9 a.m. – 1 p.m.
Fellowship Hall, St. Ansgar Lutheran Church, Minneapolis
*Enter by the alley door (ramp)*

**Bring us what's broken. Bring yourself too.**

Some years back my 1970s Hamilton Beach mixer quit working in the church kitchen, and Marv Okafor had it running again in twenty minutes. I kept thinking about how much we throw away that only needs a screw or a new cord — and how much of that is really just somebody's neighbor who'd welcome the chance to be useful. The church council approved this last week, and I'll admit it: I'm thrilled.

Fix-It Saturday is open to the whole neighborhood. You don't need to be a member of anything, there's no sign-up, and there's no fee. Bring one item per person to start so the line keeps moving: a toaster, a lamp, a bike, a torn coat, a dull knife, a laptop that won't boot. Coffee and kringle are on us. Please bring the broken toaster and stay for coffee.

We have fixers for: small appliances; lamps; bikes; clothing mending; knife sharpening; and laptops and phones (a retired tech volunteer). The mending table belongs to Doris Lindqvist, 84, who has darned socks for this parish since the Carter years and asked to run it herself.

We need more fixers — especially anyone who can do vacuums or zippers. If you're handy, come early with your tools and claim a table.

Donations to the food shelf are welcome but never expected. This is good neighboring, plain and simple: no strings, and nobody will preach at you.

Then it's the first Saturday of every month through spring — January 2, February 6, March 6, April 3 — same time, same place.

Questions, or to lend a hand:
St. Ansgar church office · office@stansgarlutheran.example · 612-555-0148

---

Three small things to check before it goes out:

- The `.example` address is a placeholder domain — confirm the real church email so the printed flier isn't dead in the coffee shops' hands.
- I've given Doris's age on the flier since you asked for it, but you may want to run it by her; "has darned socks for this parish since the Carter years" carries the same warmth without printing her age.
- The retired tech volunteer is described without a name. Give me the name and I'll add a line for him.

I also listed the follow-up dates (Jan 2, Feb 6, Mar 6, Apr 3) so the library can decide whether to display it beyond December — say the word if you'd rather keep those off the flier for now.
